post.title: Unmarried? Your deed could cost you $25,000
post.ig:
Unmarried and buying a home? Your deed could cost you $25,000.
Unmarried partners usually can't rely on divorce law to split a home.
Joint tenancy: equal shares, and the survivor gets it all. Tenants in common: shares can be unequal if the deed says so, and pass to each owner's heirs.
Example: one partner puts $60,000 of an $80,000 down payment. On $100,000 of equity, equal shares pay them $50,000; a 75/25 split written on the deed pays $75,000.
Sources: NAR 2025 Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers (unmarried couples were 11% of first-time buyers); Nolo; FindLaw. Rules vary by state.
